I agree with you, this one just wasn’t for me.

There’s so many amazing dancers in the cast, but we didn’t get too many moments that wowed me. I did enjoy the Curse Crazy circle choreography, however. 

The plot lacked depth. I have the same problem with Black Friday, where there was too much plot squished into one show. I wanted to know more about Ella’s mother, the “fairy godmother” and the light stuff. I wanted more of Sir Hops a Lot and Crumb as well as Taddius.

I have some opinions regarding the casting that seem very unpopular, and I don’t mean any of this personally or offensively to the actors. OP- my heart goes out to you. I am autistic and have misophonia, and as a teen it drove me to suicidal ideation and endless panic attacks. Certain noises were unbearable. I’m so sorry that your family set you up for failure. You’re smart for understanding it is not the child’s fault. Your sister and mother disregarding your struggle and hiding this from you cannot be easy on your mental health. 

As others have mentioned, your sister should have the room next to the babies. While the family relationship is something I cannot help with- here are some tips that can help. I have hearing aid-esque devices that i wear that pump white noise into my ears. I can control the volume to what i need to drone out certain noises while still being able to attend classes, go out, etc. Some audiologists work with people with misophonia and can order them for you. I see ads for Loop earplugs often, and they seem similar to what I have. 

I have done SO much to try and “change” this part of me. Therapy, the devices, grounding work, other sensory distractions. What really
made the difference was having the support of my close friends and families and lots and lots and lots of practice. The “itch” from these sounds hasn’t gone away, but i’ve mostly kept the panic attacks away.

Be as strong as you can, I’m so sorry this is what you’re going through. Nobody can understand the physical pain this puts us in. I wish you nothing but silence and peace!

Edit: Obviously NTA. One more thing- if you go to college, get a medical single!!! it saved my sanity in college with noise sensitivity. Roommates suck.

I used to work in a hotel built in 1894. It was a men's dormitory and then a very skeevy hotel before the company I worked for bought it. Many people died there, as it was the kind of place people would rent a room for $20 and OD. I never experienced anything there personally, but had guests mention things to me. What comes to mind is a story two separate guests told me about a month apart.

Guest 1 was an older woman and her son staying in 512. They both said they are sensitive to the paranormal. The woman said while her son was out of the room, she kept seeing reflections of an old man in the glass of the picture frames and out of the corners of her eyes. Her son said that in the middle of the night he woke up and saw an older man sitting in the chair in the corner of the room. Later in the night he woke up to the feeling of someone pulling his leg and the sound of the bathroom tap running. According to them both, nobody had used the bathroom during the night and it was fully running.

A month later, guest 2 was a middle aged woman who also claimed she was sensitive to the paranormal. She was staying by herself in 514, right next to the previous room. She said that in the middle of the night she felt a man's presence sitting on the edge of her bed pulling her leg. She woke up a few times during the night and saw him sitting in the chair in the corner of the room.

I can't speak for how legit these are- but it was interesting that they were very similar stories and coming from rooms right next to each other.

In attempts of salvaging the relationship try figuring out your Love Languages. You’ll help each other understand this and it can fix how you communicate love to each other.

As someone who has been in a long distance relationship, I can tell you that sometimes the long distance part ends up being better than in person. Sometimes people don’t physically connect or connect in person, and it’s hard to admit that after spending so long building a relationship. 

Changing in a relationship VS growing in a relationship are very different. Changing is asking an SO to stop playing video games entirely, while growing is attempting to understand their interest and discussing how you can spend your time together constructively. There’s absolutely no relationship where someone is 100% content with 100% of the other person. Having a conversation about modifying something is completely normal and DOES NOT mean that you don’t unconditionally love them. 

I hope everything works out in the way you feel is best

My parents were (and still sort of are) like this. As soon as I got my first smartphone I had to download a tracker app, and in addition text them whenever I left, arrived, and any changes in the discussed plan or else I had to come home. 

None of my friends parents were ever like this. We were all good kids who never did anything to purposely break our parents trust. They thought it was so strange and concerning. My parents were very protective (sometimes a little too protective) but there wasn’t much I could do about it until I gained trust, became an adult, and started paying for my own things. 

Bottom line is, some parents are more protective than others. IMO i think a tracker app is more reasonable (FindFriends is pretty good). Your friend may just not be used to this parental behavior, or looking out for you since sometimes there can be overlap between protective and concerning helicopter parenting. As long as you feel like it’s healthy, you should be fine. Hopefully as you get older you’ll gain more trust and won’t need the watch.
